        self.assertEqual(dedupe(["banana", "apple", "banana"]), ["banana", "apple"])
        self.assertEqual(dedupe(["b", "a", "b", "c", "a"]), ["b", "a", "c"])
        # Strings chosen so a set()-based implementation would reorder them.
        self.assertEqual(dedupe(["peer", "input", "hurry", "peer"]),

        self.assertEqual(dedupe(["x", "y", "x", "y", "x"]), ["x", "y"])
        self.assertEqual(dedupe(["same", "same", "same"]), ["same"])

    def test_unique_elements_all_kept(self):
        self.assertEqual(dedupe(["a", "b", "c"]), ["a", "b", "c"])

    def test_single_element(self):
        self.assertEqual(dedupe(["only"]), ["only"])

    def test_empty_list_returns_empty_list_not_none(self):
        result = dedupe([])

        self.assertEqual(result, [])

                    "abc",            # str is iterable but not a list
                    None,
                    42):
            with self.subTest(items=bad):
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    dedupe(bad)

    # --- criterion 5: returns a NEW list and never mutates the input ---------

    def test_input_not_mutated_and_result_is_new_list(self):
        items = ["alpha", "beta", "alpha", "gamma"]

        result = dedupe(items)

        self.assertIsNot(result, items, "result must be a NEW list, not the input object")
        self.assertEqual(items, snapshot, "input list must not be mutated")

        # Any permutation of the input by a set/hash order must not survive.
        expected = ["banana", "apple", "cherry"]
        self.assertEqual(dedupe(expected + ["banana", "apple"]), expected)
